questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The Metropolitan Police's response to the 1858 summer riots in London
The architecture of Abbey Mills and Crossness pumping stations
The discovery of germ theory and John Snow's Broad Street map
The 1858 Thames stench and how Bazalgette's sewers solved London's sewage crisis
questions.explain: It covers the Great Stink, the sewage background, and Bazalgette's sewer system.

questions.q: What two embankments besides Victoria and Chelsea did Bazalgette's plan include?
options: Albert Embankment
Crossness Embankment
Westminster Embankment
Thames Embankment
questions.explain: The plan introduced the Victoria, Chelsea and Albert Embankments.

questions.q: What did the Metropolis Management Act do?
options: Replaced the Metropolitan Commission of Sewers with the Metropolitan Board of Works
Required all new buildings to be connected to a sewer
Appointed Joseph Bazalgette as chief engineer of the city
Transferred control of the sewers to a national public health agency
questions.explain: The Metropolis Management Act 1855 replaced the commission with the Metropolitan Board of Works, which took control of the sewers.

questions.q: What did Michael Faraday do to test the Thames in 1855?
options: Sampled the fish living near the bridges
Measured the river's temperature at midday
Boiled river water and tested the steam
Dropped white paper into the river
questions.explain: He dropped pieces of white paper into the river to test its opacity.

questions.q: Why did flushing the sewers regularly make the Thames worse?
options: It discharged more sewage into the river
It blocked the old brick pipes with debris
It spread miasma into homes and cesspits
It killed the fish living below the bridges
questions.explain: Chadwick and Simon flushed sewers out of miasma fear, which resulted in more sewage in the Thames.
